Good morning, Mrs Harper. I'm Doctor Ellis. Thanks for coming in. What's brought you to see me today?
Morning, doctor. It's this chest pain. It started about three weeks ago and it just hasn't settled.
Tell me about the pain. Where exactly do you feel it?
Right here, in the middle of my chest. Sometimes it goes up into my jaw and down my left arm.
And when does it come on?
Mostly when I'm walking up the hill to the shops. If I stop and rest it eases off after a few minutes.
How would you describe it? Sharp, dull, crushing?
Like a heavy weight pressing down. Not stabbing. More of a tightness.
On a scale of one to ten, how bad does it get?
At its worst, maybe a seven. Usually it's a four or five.
Does anything else come with it? Breathlessness, sweating, nausea?
I do get short of breath. And last Tuesday I felt quite sick and clammy with it.
Have you had any pain at rest, or anything that woke you at night?
No, nothing at night. Only when I'm moving about.
Any swelling in your ankles, or palpitations?
My ankles have been a bit puffy in the evenings, yes. No fluttering though.
Let's go through your background. Do you have any diagnosed conditions?
High blood pressure, for about twelve years. And they told me I was borderline diabetic two years ago.
What medication are you taking at the moment?
Ramipril, five milligrams in the morning. And atorvastatin, twenty milligrams at night.
Are you taking those every day?
Most days. I forget the statin sometimes, maybe twice a week.
Penicillin. I came out in a rash when I was a girl.
I gave up four years ago. I smoked about fifteen a day for thirty years before that.
A glass of wine with dinner, maybe four nights a week.
Is there heart disease in the family?
My father had a heart attack at fifty-eight. He survived it but he was never the same.
That's important, thank you. Let me examine you now. Can you sit forward for me?
Your blood pressure is one hundred and fifty-two over ninety-four. Pulse is eighty-eight and regular.
Heart sounds are normal, no murmurs. Chest is clear. There's mild pitting oedema to both ankles.
Is that the swelling you meant?
Yes, and it's mild. Now, I want to be straightforward with you about what I think is going on.
The pattern you describe — pain on exertion that settles with rest, radiating to the jaw and arm — is typical of angina.
No. Angina is the heart muscle not getting enough blood when it's working hard. It's a warning, not a heart attack.
It's treatable, and the fact that you came in is the right thing. But I don't want to guess, so we'll investigate.
I'm going to arrange an ECG today, and bloods — full blood count, kidney function, lipids, and an HbA1c for the diabetes.
I'm also referring you to the rapid access chest pain clinic. They'll see you within two weeks.
Two weeks. What do I do in the meantime?
I'm starting you on a glyceryl trinitrate spray. Two sprays under the tongue when the pain comes.
Sit down before you use it. If the pain is not gone fifteen minutes after a second dose, call an ambulance.
I'm also starting aspirin, seventy-five milligrams daily, and increasing your atorvastatin to eighty milligrams at night.
Will the aspirin upset my stomach?
It can. Take it with food. If you get indigestion or any black stools, tell us straight away.
And should I stop walking up that hill?
Don't stop being active, but don't push through pain. Walk on the flat, stop when it comes on, use the spray.
What about my work? I do three shifts a week at the garden centre.
Lifting heavy bags is the part I'd avoid for now. Light duties until the clinic has seen you.
One more thing. Please take the statin every day, not most days. It matters more than almost anything else here.
I will. I've got a pill box, I'll start using it properly.
Good. So: ECG and bloods today, chest pain clinic within two weeks, GTN spray as needed, aspirin and the higher statin.
And the red flag: pain at rest, or pain that doesn't go after two sprays and fifteen minutes, is a nine-nine-nine call.
Got it. Thank you, doctor. I feel better knowing what it is.
You're welcome. The nurse will do the ECG now. I'll ring you with the blood results on Friday.
